newsitem.title: USA: Wiltek unit to merge with Splintercom.
newsitem.headline: Wiltek unit to merge with Splintercom.

text.p: Wiltek Inc said Monday it has signed an agreement with SplinterCom LLC to create a new subsidiary that focuses on developing voice recognition and computer telephone integration products.

Upon closing, SplinterCom designees will make up a majority of Wiltek's five-member board. SplinterCom's founder and chief executive, James Ackerly, will become chairman and chief executive of Wiltek, and David Teitelman will remain Wiltek president.
The agreement calls for Wiltek to acquire SplinterCom's assets and $3.5 million in cash that SplinterCom raised in a private financing, in exchange for 3.5 million shares of Wiltek shares.
SplinterCom will acquire another 746,950 shares of Wiltek from three of the company's departing board members for $0.85 per share, Teitelman said.
SplinterCom is a developmental stage company and is the first spin off of the Internet Splinter Group, an association of technology professionals that develops and promotes promising technologies.
Wiltek provides electronic messaging, enhanced directory synchronization, fax transport and consulting services to corporate accounts worldwide.
The merger follows a letter of intent signed between the companies last May.
